HomeEssentials Inc. - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, everyone, and welcome to the HomeEssentials Inc. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, instructions for queuing up can be found by pressing the * key followed by 1 on your touchtone phone. Please also note, today's event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, and thank you for joining us today to discuss HomeEssentials Inc.'s results for the Q3 2024. Joining me on today’s call are Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Hargrove, Chief Financial Officer; Jennifer Hale, Chief Merchandising Officer; Robert Kline, Chief Stores Officer; and Olivia Grant, Chief Marketing Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements, which are subject to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

With that, I’ll turn the call over to Sarah Thompson.

Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Thank you, Alex. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I’m pleased to report HomeEssentials Inc.'s performance for the Q3 2024. We continued to execute on our strategic priorities and delivered solid results despite the challenging macroeconomic environment.

Our comparable sales grew 2.8% on a two-year stack basis, with traffic up 1.2% and average ticket expanding 1.5%, fueled by our Everyday Low Price strategy and targeted promotions in apparel and home essentials. Today, I'll touch on several key aspects of our performance, including our financial outlook, digital marketing effectiveness, marketing and advertising expense trends, labor costs and store payroll leverage, store remodel and renovation plans, traffic versus ticket breakdown, and supply chain efficiency improvements.

We are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Michael Hargrove to provide more details on our financial results.

Michael Hargrove, Chief Financial Officer:
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning. I'll provide a more detailed review of our financial performance for the Q3 2024.

Our total revenue for the quarter was $8.35 billion, a 2.8% increase compared to the same period last year. Gross margin was 28.7%, primarily driven by lower markdowns in softlines as inventory levels normalized. Operating expenses were $1.8 billion, representing 21.5% of revenue. Net income was $320 million, or $0.92 per share. We generated $450 million in cash flow from operations. Inventory levels are currently at 10 weeks of supply, down from 12.5 weeks a year ago.

We are maintaining a strong balance sheet and are well positioned to invest in our growth initiatives. As we wrap up a solid quarter, let me turn to our outlook for the balance of the fiscal year and into FY2025.

Starting with Q4 guidance, we expect consolidated net sales in the range of $8.2 billion to $8.5 billion, representing flat to 2% comp sales growth excluding the 53rd week impact from last year. On an adjusted basis, we're guiding to 1% to 3% comps growth, with digital sales – which now represent 18% of total revenue – accelerating to mid-single-digit growth on the strength of our BOPIS fulfillment, where curbside pickup accounted for 45% of e-comm orders in Q3. Gross margin is projected at 28.5% to 29.0%, a 20 basis point expansion sequentially, benefiting from lower markdowns in softlines as inventory levels normalize to 10 weeks of supply by quarter-end, down from 12.5 weeks a year ago. Adjusted operating income should come in at $450 million to $500 million, with SG&A as a percentage of sales flat at 21.5%, reflecting disciplined labor scheduling via our AI-powered workforce management tool, similar to what we've seen at peers like Target with their Mosaic platform.

EPS guidance for Q4 is $0.85 to $0.95 on an adjusted basis, incorporating a tax rate of 24.5% and roughly 10 million more shares outstanding due to our ongoing $500 million share repurchase authorization. Capex will total $350 million for the year, focused on 50 store remodels emphasizing experiential zones – think interactive kitchen demos in our home department, akin to Williams-Sonoma's model – and expanding micro-fulfillment centers to 25 units, enabling same-day delivery in 80% of our top 100 DMAs.

For full FY2024, we're raising the midpoint of our guidance: net sales of $32.5 billion to $33.0 billion, up from our prior $32.0 billion to $32.8 billion range; adjusted operating margin of 5.8% to 6.2%; and adjusted EPS of $3.40 to $3.60, up 15% at the midpoint from FY2023. This reflects better-than-expected category performance, particularly in consumables up 4.2% comps on volume, offsetting softer discretionary categories like electronics, which faced headwinds from a high single-digit decline in TV unit sales amid a post-Olympics lull.

Looking further out to FY2025, we see a path to 3% to 5% comps growth, accelerating in the back half as consumer confidence stabilizes around current Index levels of 105 and real wage growth holds above 2%. Revenue should grow 4% to 6% on a two-year CAGR basis, driven by square footage optimization: we're planning 20 net new stores in high-growth Sunbelt markets like Texas and Florida, where we've seen 5%+ comps in Q3 versus flat in the Northeast, while closing 15 underperforming locations in legacy malls reminiscent of the JCPenney rationalization playbook. This keeps door growth at 1%, but with productivity gains from our RFID tagging initiative now covering 90% of inventory, reducing shrinkage to 1.1% of sales.

Margin expansion remains a core focus, targeting 150 basis points of gross margin improvement over two years through private label penetration – our GoodValue brand now at 28% of sales, up from 24%, with 40%+ margins versus national brands – and supply chain efficiencies from our Memphis DC automation upgrade, which shaved 50 basis points off freight costs in Q3. Operating margin should expand to 6.5% to 7.0% in FY2025, with SG&A leverage from omnichannel synergies; for instance, store-fulfilled e-comm now drives 60% of digital orders, boosting store traffic by 2% in pilot locations.

Free cash flow outlook is robust at $1.2 billion for FY2025, supporting $800 million in dividends and buybacks while funding $400 million in capex. We're also advancing our tech stack with generative AI for personalized assortments, piloting in 200 stores to lift conversion 1.5 points, much like Walmart's Search & Reimagine efforts.

Regionally, the Sunbelt continues to outperform with 4.5% comps, fueled by population in-migration and lower regional unemployment at 3.2%, while the Midwest faces pressure from ag sector softness, limiting comps to 1%. Internationally, our 50 Canadian stores expect 2% comps in local currency, supported by CAD/USD stability.

Strategically, we're positioning as the value leader in brick-and-mortar with hybrid relevance: think "stores as hubs" for services like device repair partnerships with Best Buy-style Geek Squad analogs, capturing the $50 billion services TAM. Risks include persistent inflation above 2.5% crimping discretionary spend, potential port strikes echoing 2023 disruptions, and a consumer pivot to discounters like Dollar General if unemployment ticks up. But opportunities abound in housing turnover – up 8% YoY per NAR data – driving home refresh comps, and our loyalty program, with 65 million active members, yielding 3x the spend of non-members.

Now, turning to labor costs and store payroll leverage, which has been a critical driver of our operating margin expansion. In Q3, total store labor costs came in at $285 million, up 3.2% year-over-year, well below our comparable store sales growth of 2.8%. This delivered strong payroll leverage of 120 basis points, with store payroll as a percentage of sales declining to 12.4% from 13.6% in the prior-year period. Sales per labor hour rose 4.1% to $185 per hour across our 1,250 stores, driven by traffic recovery and disciplined hours management. We reduced store labor hours by 1.8% YoY while comp traffic was up 1.2%. This productivity gain stands out amid wage inflation averaging 4.7% across our hourly associate base, in line with peers like Target and TJX.

Post-COVID structural shifts have stabilized turnover at 65% annually, but skilled roles remain challenging, especially in Sunbelt markets. Wage pressures vary: Northeast and California at $19.50/hour, 12% above average, versus $17.80 in Midwest and Southeast. Texas and Florida stores delivered SPLH of $212/hour, up 6.3% YoY.

We've leaned into technology like AI-powered workforce management with UKG Pro across 85% of stores, optimizing schedules with hyper-local forecasting incorporating weather, events, and competitor data. This cut overtime by 22% to 3.1% of hours, improved adherence to 92%, and reduced understaffing by 35%. Our Peak Hour Precision initiative uses computer vision at 400 stores to adjust staffing, boosting basket size by 1.2 items. Full-time to part-time mix shifted to 42:58, with retention bonuses lifting tenure to 2.3 years.

Ahead, with 4-6% back-half comps, we target another 100 basis points leverage assuming 4.2% wage inflation. Mitigants include robotic stocking pilots and Essentials Academy training for omnichannel tasks.

On supply chain efficiency improvements, year-over-year we've reduced total supply chain costs by 18%, from 12.4% to 10.2% of sales, yielding $142 million in savings on $8.35 billion revenue. Inventory turns accelerated to 7.8x from 6.2x, carrying 22% less inventory at 48 days supply, with fill rates at 98.5% and BOPIS service at 97%, fueling 14% omnichannel comp growth.

This stems from our $450 million ForgeForward program, using stores as micro-hubs. Manhattan WMS and Oracle SCM with AI demand sensing improved forecast accuracy 28% to 92%, slashing safety stock 35% in volatile categories. Automation in 65% of 28 DCs with AutoStore boosted productivity 40%, cutting labor per case to $0.17. Blockchain on 20% private-label SKUs reduced disputes to 48 hours.

Regionally, U.S. nearshoring cut lead times to 22 days, improving transit 19%. Canada rail partnerships saved $18 million; Europe localized 55% assortments, cutting costs 14%. Asia diversified sourcing 25% from China.

Store network enables same-day for 85% customers; $120 million CapEx expands micro-fulfillment. Sustainability cuts Scope 3 17%. These gains expanded gross margins 110 bps to 32.4%, contributing 40% to EPS beat.

We're not done; Phase 2 targets 10-12% further reduction by FY25.

Now, I'd like to hand it over to Jennifer Hale, our Chief Merchandising Officer, to discuss our new product lines, followed by Robert Kline to discuss store operations, and then Olivia Grant to discuss marketing initiatives.

Jennifer Hale, Chief Merchandising Officer:
Thank you, Michael. This quarter, we launched our refreshed Essentials Refresh kitchen line, which has seen strong uptake with viral traction from user-generated content, contributing to a 15% lift in related SKUs. We've also expanded our GoodValue private label to 28% of sales, delivering 40%+ margins. We are excited about the potential of this new product and other upcoming launches, particularly in home furnishings tied to housing turnover trends.

Robert Kline, Chief Stores Officer:
Thank you, Jennifer. We continue to focus on improving the customer experience in our stores. We have implemented our accelerated remodel program and are seeing positive results, including 4.2% SSS uplift in remodeled units.

We're entering a multi-year remodel cycle with 42 completions in Q3, year-to-date 78, up 35% YoY. FY2024 CapEx $450 million for 180 stores next year, scaling to 250 by FY2026. Per-store $2.1 million for full prototypes, $850k for express.

Key pillars: zone-based layout with Discovery Plaza kiosks boosting app downloads 22%; Lifestyle Hub vignettes lifting basket 15%; Fulfillment Fortress expanding BOPIS 40%; Community Corner increasing dwell 18 minutes.

Tech includes LED retrofits saving 30% energy, RFID to 96% availability, computer vision for 2.5-point conversion lift, Just Walk Out pilots reducing queues 65%.

Sunbelt prioritizes HVAC and porch zones, AUV up 12%; Northeast cozy enclaves and EV charging; Midwest value bulk; California green builds.

ROI: 3-year payback at 22% IRR, +5-7% SSS perpetuity, $75 million EBITDA by FY2027. Positions us as experiential hubs, reducing turnover 18%.

On traffic versus ticket, our 1.2% traffic gain paired with 1.5% ticket expansion reflects balanced execution: traffic from omnichannel lifts and remodels, ticket from EDLP and promotions in apparel/home.

Olivia Grant, Chief Marketing Officer:
Thank you, Robert. Our marketing efforts, including the Essentials Refresh campaign, have increased brand awareness and driven results.

I'm pleased to highlight our digital marketing effectiveness amid a resilient but challenged landscape. Digital channels delivered 6.2x ROAS in Q3, up from 4.8x YoY and 5.5x Q2, our strongest since pre-pandemic. Total digital spend $145 million, up 18% YoY, 22% of budget after cutting traditional TV/print 25%. Generated $900 million revenue, 28% lift in BOPIS.

Paid search 42% spend, 8.1x ROAS via Google Performance Max, top-of-funnel +35%, CPC -15%. Social 30%, 5.4x via Meta Advantage+ and TikTok Spark Ads, 22% store visits lift.

CDP with Tealium live 85%, reduced CAC 19% to $28, 32% geofencing incrementality, 41% traffic uplift in Chicago. Southeast 7.1x ROAS with Uber Eats pilots; Midwest 5.3x countered by SEO; Europe 4.2x recovered via BigQuery.

Retail media network generated $12 million from CPG; 15% next-year budget to CTV; multi-touch shows email/SMS 24% to store sales.

Digital accelerates physical stores amid 2.1% industry traffic decline.

On marketing and advertising expense trends, total expenses $178 million, up 15% YoY, 2.8% of sales versus 2.4%. Full-year 2.6-2.8%. Digital/performance 68% of budget, up from 55%; traditional down 22% to $32 million.

Digital $98 million up 28%, paid social $42 million, search $28 million, Connect network $28 million revenue share. Blended ROAS 4.2x. AI personalization CAC $22, LTV $312 up 8%.

Omnichannel 42% spend to BOPIS 18% sales; Performance Max +22% traffic. Connect offsets 16% spend, 9% impulse uplift. Influencers $12 million up 35%, 17% comp lift; loyalty $18 million, redemptions 28%.

U.S. $128 million up 18%, +2.4% comps; Canada $22 million up 16%; Europe flat €18 million, CTV 4.8x; Asia A$8 million up 25%, 6.1x ROAS.

Traffic First framework combats showrooming; MER $112 up from $102. Q4 up 20% QoQ, AR pilots. Positions resiliently.

Now, let's open the line for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for questions: press * then 1. Our first question comes from Laura Chen with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Laura Chen (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of persistent inflation on your sales?

Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Good morning, Laura. Inflation above 2.5% is crimping discretionary spend, particularly in electronics with high single-digit TV declines post-Olympics. However, consumables comped 4.2% on volume, and housing turnover up 8% YoY drives home refresh. Our EDLP and GoodValue private label at 28% sales with higher margins mitigate this, while Sunbelt outperformance at 4.5% comps shows resilience in lower-unemployment areas.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Patel with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

David Patel (JPMorgan):
What are your expectations for same-store sales growth in the next quarter?

Michael Hargrove, Chief Financial Officer:
Thanks, David. For Q4, adjusted comps 1% to 3%, with digital mid-single digits. FY2025 path to 3-5%, accelerating back half on stabilizing confidence at Index 105 and 2%+ wage growth. Sunbelt 20 new stores, Northeast closures, RFID shrinkage to 1.1%.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Ross with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Emily Ross (Morgan Stanley):
Can you elaborate on the supply chain improvements?

Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Absolutely, Emily. We've cut costs 18% to 10.2% of sales, inventory turns 7.8x, 22% less stock at 48 days. AI forecasting 92% accuracy, DC automation productivity +40%, nearshoring lead times to 22 days. Store micro-hubs enable same-day for 85%, with Phase 2 targeting 10-12% more savings.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Kevin Lee with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Kevin Lee (Barclays):
What is the impact from the loyalty program?

Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Great question, Kevin. 65 million active members spend 3x non-members. Personalized offers via SMS/push at 28% redemption, CAC $22-28, LTV $312. Drives 60% store-fulfilled digital, +2% traffic in pilots, amplifying comps.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sophia Nguyen with Citi. Please go ahead.

Sophia Nguyen (Citi):
Thanks. On store remodels, what's the ROI timeline and regional prioritization?

Robert Kline, Chief Stores Officer:
Sophia, remodels deliver 3-year payback at 22% IRR, +5-7% SSS perpetuity, 15% traffic growth. $450 million FY24 CapEx, 180 stores FY25. Sunbelt first for housing/population, AUV +12%; Northeast EV/cozy; Midwest value; California green.

Operator:
Thank you. That concludes today's questions.

Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, we are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain focused on executing our long-term strategy. Thank you for your continued support.

Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations:
This concludes today's call. Thank you for joining us.
